policy_title: Guarantee NHS Dentist Access for Urgent Care
stated: Guarantee access to an NHS dentist for everyone needing urgent and emergency care, ending DIY dentistry and ‘dental deserts’ by: Bringing dentists back to the NHS from the private sector (fixing the broken NHS dental contract and using flexible commissioning), introducing an emergency scheme to guarantee access to free NHS dental check-ups for eligible groups (children, new mothers, pregnant individuals, low-income individuals), and guaranteeing appointments for all who need a dental check before commencing surgery, chemotherapy or transplant.

source.quote: Guarantee access to an NHS dentist for everyone needing urgent and emergency care, ending DIY dentistry and ‘dental deserts’. Guarantee access to an NHS dentist for everyone needing urgent and emergency care by: Bringing dentists back to the NHS from the private sector by fixing the broken NHS dental contract and using flexible commissioning to meet patient needs. Introducing an emergency scheme to guarantee access to free NHS dental check-ups for those already eligible: children, new mothers, those who are pregnant and those on low incomes. Guaranteeing appointments for all those who need a dental check before commencing surgery, chemotherapy or transplant.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets NHS dental access — waiting times, capacity, and coverage for urgent/emergency care and vulnerable groups — core healthcare access indicators.

The emergency scheme explicitly targets low-income individuals, children, pregnant people and new mothers for free check-ups, directly narrowing the income-correlated gap in dental health access; the 'dental deserts' framing also addresses regional inequality.

Introducing a new emergency free check-up scheme and restructuring NHS dental commissioning to attract dentists back from private practice represents a material spending commitment; whether it is funded or involves additional borrowing has a concrete effect on the public-finance position.

membership_note: The policy's primary effect is on healthcare access (O3), with a targeted distributional dimension (O14) and a real but unquantified fiscal commitment (O12). Cost-of-living (O2) is tempted by 'ending DIY dentistry' reducing out-of-pocket costs, but this flows through healthcare access rather than the price of food/energy/bills essentials, so it sits cleanly in O3 rather than O2.
